subject: Archaeology
title: How Sites Are Discovered
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on How Sites Are Discovered.

hook.text: Most archaeological sites are found by accident — farmers plowing fields, builders digging foundations.

buildup.text: The Terracotta Army was found by farmers digging a well. Lascaux Cave was found by teenagers chasing a runaway dog.

discovery.text: Professional surveys also find sites. Archaeologists walk fields in lines, scanning the ground for pottery and flint.

twist.text: Construction projects destroy more sites than they reveal. Most countries require surveys before building.

climax.text: Satellite imagery and LiDAR now find hidden sites from space. Thousands of unknown ruins have been spotted from above.

punchline.text: A dog, a well, a satellite — archaeology starts with someone noticing something.

quiz.question: How are most archaeological sites initially discovered?
options: By professional archaeologists conducting planned excavations
By accident — farmers, builders, or people stumbling on remains
By satellite imagery scanning from orbit
